messages.subject: Saving images with svg format
parts:

Loading required package: grid
Loading required package: reshape
Loading required package: plyr
Loading required package: digest

Saving 12" x 7.29" image
Error: 'svg' is not an exported object from 'namespace:grDevices'
 
I have come across following thread "http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/f27468b5e428374d/e5f8ab32b9b1adc2?lnk=gst&q=save+svg+format#e5f8ab32b9b1adc2" however still it seems unsolved. Thanks,

messages.author: 4e69b94a09c8cf3b
messages.subject: Re: Saving images with svg format
parts:
I have successfully used grDevices::svg and Cairo::CairoSVG to print ggplot to.  I do something along the lines of

svg(paste(imagedir,"aaa.svg",sep=""))

ggplot(static) +
  aes(x=x, y=y, group=factor(abs(depth_cm)), color=pawcx, size=pawcx) +
  geom_point() +
  coord_equal() +
  facet_grid(depth_cm ~.) +
  scale_color_gradientn(colour=brewer.pal(6, "YlOrRd"))

dev.off()


I use inkview/inkscape to view the svg.

parts:
Hi:

A little while back, I took a png file created from ggplot() through ggsave(), imported it into Inkscape, played with it a bit and saved it as svg with no problem; a few others have mentioned doing similar things with other vector graphics formats.

I'm certainly no expert on creating svg graphics within R per se, but the cairoDevice package has a function Cairo_svg() which apparently opens up an svg device within Cairo. I don't have it loaded on my system, but my limited understanding is that it needs the (R)Gtk+ toolkit to be pre-installed. If anyone here works with Cairo and knows how to set it up on Windows, this would be a good time to chime in - I may not be the only one curious about it :)

FWIW,
Dennis
